# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐 ✌]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through gestures, since Mute can't speak to me directly in a way I'd understand differently - wait, actually Mute *can* speak and I *can* hear speech from Mute. But this turn Mute only gestured. Let me think about what info I have: a display showing 0, a blue light, and three wires (green, yellow, red). Mute has the manual and is using gestures (which I can see) to try to convey something to me, since gestures aren't heard by Blind but are seen by me.

The gesture sequence is: 👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐 ✌. This could be encoding numbers via finger-count-like symbols (☝=1, ✌=2, 🖐=5) or could be indicating wire order/selection. Without an established code yet, I can't decode this reliably. I should establish communication - tell Mute what I see, since Mute can hear my speech, and let Mute (who has the manual) match it against instructions. I should also flag that I received a gesture but don't have a shared code yet.

Since it's Mute, Blind, Deaf order, and I go last, my speech this turn will reach nobody this round (round is over after me), but it will reach them at the start of next round. So I should speak now to describe the bomb, which both Mute and Blind will receive at the start of next round.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I saw Mute gesture but we have no code yet - Mute, please speak plainly next turn about what the manual says to do, since I can hear you.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤙 ☝ 🖐 🤘]

Mute is still only gesturing to me, never speaking - which is odd since Mute *can* speak (Mute just cannot touch the bomb; speaking is allowed for Mute... wait, let me recheck the rules. Actually checking the table again: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute literally cannot speak at all! I misread that earlier. Mute can only communicate via gestures. That means my instruction to "speak plainly" was impossible for Mute to follow.

So Mute's only channel to me is gestures, and Mute's only channel to Blind is... nothing, since gestures aren't heard and Mute can't speak. Wait - Blind cannot see gestures either. So Mute cannot communicate with Blind directly at all! Mute can only reach me (Deaf) via gestures. And I can speak to both Mute (who can't hear me since Mute isn't deaf... wait Mute has no hearing restriction listed, only "cannot speak, or touch bomb"). Let me recheck: Mute's restrictions are "Speak, or touch the bomb" - so Mute CAN hear. Good, so I can talk to Mute.

So the information flow is: Mute knows the manual, gestures to me (Deaf). I see the bomb and can speak to both Mute and Blind. Blind can act but can't see or hear speech-independent gestures, only hears speech from Mute... wait Blind cannot hear at all? Let me check: Blind's cannot list: "See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." No restriction on hearing! So Blind CAN hear speech. 

So: Mute gestures to me, I translate/relay via speech to Blind who acts. This makes sense as the intended chain.

Now I need to decode Mute's gestures. Symbols so far:
Turn1: 👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🖐 ☝ 🖐 ✌
Turn2: 👍 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤙 ☝ 🖐 🤘

Common prefix: 👍 👊 ☝ ✌ then differs at position 5, then ☝ 🖐 then differs at position 8.

This looks like it could be a fixed preamble (maybe identifying itself or a constant instruction) plus variable parts reflecting current bomb state (which hasn't changed - display still 0, light still blue, wires same). Since the bomb state is identical between turns, but gestures differ slightly, maybe Mute is spelling out instructions letter by letter across turns (like a slow message), not encoding bomb state.

I should tell Mute what I see and ask them to confirm/guide using consistent gesture-per-symbol mapping, and relay to Blind that we're still decoding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here again. I see your gestures but we have no shared code for them yet. Bomb still shows display 0, blue light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red - unchanged since last turn. Can you gesture one instruction at a time, very simply, like pointing to a wire number or a single action? Try just one or two symbols per turn so I can match them to what changes.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Bomb shows display 0, blue light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red, unchanged. Still working out Mute's gesture code, please hold off touching anything until we confirm.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Good, Mute simplified to a single gesture this turn: 🤟 (love-you sign / "I Love You" ASL sign). This could be an attempt to establish a simple code - maybe using ASL letter signs? 🤟 is the ASL sign for "I love you" but individual gesture symbols in this game don't have inherent meaning until we assign it. Mute seems to be trying to respond to my request for simpler signals.

Since I asked Mute to point to a wire number or single action, this single gesture might be an answer. But I don't know what 🤟 means yet without more context. I should acknowledge receipt and ask Mute to build a simple numbering system - e.g., "1 gesture = wire 1, 2 gestures = wire 2" etc., using something intuitive like finger-counting symbols (☝✌🖐 style).

Let me propose a concrete code since Mute can hear me: use ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🖐 for 5 fingers etc. Actually simplest: ask Mute to use ☝ ✌ 🤟(3?) or numbers of repeated same gesture to indicate wire number, and 👍/👎 for yes/no confirmations.

I'll propose: single tap gestures - point at nothing, but since Mute can't see the bomb, Mute is relying on the manual only, not matching bomb state. So Mute's gestures are manual-instructions, independent of what I see. I need to ask Mute to answer yes/no questions from me instead, since I know the bomb state and Mute knows the manual - so I should ask Mute questions and have them answer via simple gesture codes (👍=yes, 👎=no), which is efficient.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us use a simple code. Please answer yes or no questions with a single gesture: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. First question: does the manual say the correct wire depends on the light colour?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed: 👍 = yes, the correct wire depends on the light colour. This establishes our yes/no code works. Now I should ask more targeted questions to narrow down which wire to cut given blue light and display 0.

Let me continue building the picture with binary questions, since each round only gets one gesture from Mute to me (and I speak once, they gesture once per round - slow but works).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, understood. Light is blue right now. Does the manual say for a blue light we should cut a specific single wire, or do multiple steps apply, like check display first?")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute answered 👍 again - but my question was ambiguous (a compound "or" question), so this yes could mean either branch. I need to ask cleaner binary questions, one fact at a time.

Let me be more careful and precise now.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Sorry, that question was unclear, let me be precise. Answer only this: for a blue light, is there exactly one single wire to cut, yes or no?")
```

Confirmed: yes, exactly one single wire to cut for blue light. Now I need to identify which wire number/color. I'll ask about colors directly since that's likely how the manual encodes it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good. Now answer only this: for a blue light, is the correct wire green, yes or no?")
```

Not green. Next, ask about yellow.

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Interesting - Blind also gestured to me. But wait, Blind cannot see gestures, but Blind can *make* gestures? Let me check: Blind's restriction is "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - that's about receiving, not sending. Blind could gesture, but since I can see, I'd receive it. But this is odd since Blind doesn't know my code with Mute. Let me note it but focus on the wire deduction first: not green, not yellow, so by elimination it must be red (wire 3).

Let me confirm with Mute to be sure, and also acknowledge Blind's gesture, asking what it means since we haven't set up a code with Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="So not green, not yellow, meaning the correct wire is red, wire 3. Please confirm this with thumbs up if correct, thumbs down if not.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. I saw a gesture from you but I cannot tell what it means yet, we have no shared code for that. If you can hear me, please respond in words, do not touch any wire yet, we are close to confirming which one is safe to cut.")
```
